PullRequest.Title: Engineering - don't break SDK validation builds on BinSkim results
PullRequest.Body:
The first run of the new SDK validation definition (720), [489376](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=489376), failed Linux x64 and arm64 Compile at `Guardian: Post Analysis`. The cause was 23 existing BinSkim errors (BA3003, BA3030) in the server's native modules: `vscode-server-linux-*/node_modules/{kerberos,vsda,node-pty}/build/Release/*.node`.

## Root cause

This isn't a new finding or a target-glob gap. The product build (definition 111) scans the same binaries and gets the same results. In the Linux x64 Compile job of the 17:00 insider [489293](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=489293), BinSkim scanned the same 52 targets (22 `VSCode-*`, 15 `vscode-server-*`, 15 `vscode-server-*-web`) and the Security Analysis Report shows the same 23 active results. Its `analyzeTargetGlob` doesn't keep the server folders out on Linux.

The difference is the 1ES break policy. `v1/Stages/Stage.yml` defaults `binskim.break` to `not(and(isOfficial, tsa.enabled))`:
- **Definition 111** (official template, TSA on): `break` is false. Post Analysis excludes all 106 results "by tool filters", and they go to TSA instead.
- **Definition 720** (unofficial template, TSA off): `break` is true, so Post Analysis fails on the 23 errors.

## Change

Set the documented 1ES parameter `sdl.binskim.break: false` in `sdk-validation-build.yml`. BinSkim still runs and its results are still in the SDL logs, which matches the product build's outcome. I didn't turn on TSA, because a never-shipping validation pipeline would file duplicate TSA bugs.

## Validation

Full definition 720 run on this branch: [489454](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=489454).

> Authored with Copilot

Scenarios.Scenario: SDK validation compile and BinSkim post-analysis across the eight independent platform stages
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each compile produces binaries, then Guardian/BinSkim scans the configured native targets before the compile job can succeed. The added setting changes only whether existing findings fail post-analysis; scanning and result reporting remain on the same critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: BinSkim enumerates and analyzes compiled native binaries in the agent build directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One post-analysis scan per applicable compile job over the same target globs and binaries as before.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The identical scan and reporting ran, then existing findings failed unofficial SDK validation jobs because the default break policy was true.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The scan must still finish before a compile job completes; only its findings no longer convert completion into failure.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Guardian/1ES publishes SDL logs and results.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The same result publication per job as before; setting break:false does not add a report or scan.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Results were already generated and published before the job was marked failed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Reporting remains part of post-analysis, with no evidenced extra network operation or serialization.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number and size of compiled native .node/.exe/.dll targets per platform; Linux non-armhf scans client, server, and web-server trees. Effective cardinality is unchanged by the diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All eight top-level stages declare dependsOn: [] and can run concurrently. The diff neither adds stages nor raises parallelism; each job's post-analysis remains local to that job.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache key or cache lifecycle is changed. Cold and warm runs perform the same BinSkim scan as before, and there is no new retry or miss behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the diff changes only binskim.break, while repository target globs and all stage/job definitions are unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The external 1ES template implementation and exact scan durations are not in this repository, but the documented parameter semantics and unchanged enabled/target configuration establish that work cardinality is unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The change preserves scan cost, target count, and stage concurrency while changing only failure policy.

Scenarios.Scenario: Linux x64 Agent Host E2E validation after a compile containing known BinSkim findings
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Linux_x64_Test_AgentHostE2E depends on Linux_x64_Compile. With the prior failing post-analysis it was gated; after break:false the successful compile artifact can be downloaded and the intended E2E suite can run.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Download the compilation pipeline artifact for the dependent Linux x64 E2E job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One artifact download for the single Linux x64 Agent Host E2E job when its compile succeeds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: On the observed trigger, the compile job failed in Guardian post-analysis, so its dependent E2E job could not consume the artifact.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Newly reachable for runs that previously stopped specifically on known BinSkim findings; required for the pipeline's declared validation purpose.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run the selected Agent Host Electron E2E test suite.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selected E2E suite in one dependent Linux x64 job, independent of the number of BinSkim findings.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: It was gated when the compile was marked failed by the known BinSkim findings, though it already ran on successful validation builds without such findings.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs after successful compile and is required before Linux x64 validation completes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: A single Linux x64 compilation artifact and the selected integration-agent-host-e2e test ID; there is one dependent E2E job, not per BinSkim finding.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The E2E job is serialized behind Linux_x64_Compile. Other platform stages remain independently concurrent; the diff creates no burst or per-finding fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Test retries can skip tasks already passed in an earlier attempt, per the test template. The break-policy change adds no cache, cache miss, invalidation, or repeated-failure loop.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the explicit dependsOn and selected test ID prove reachability when compile status changes from failed to successful.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact artifact size and E2E duration are not established here, but cardinality is fixed at one dependent job and does not scale with findings.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The additional work is the bounded, pre-existing validation job that the pipeline is explicitly designed to run; the diff repairs premature failure rather than adding accidental repeated work, fan-out, or concurrency.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete one-file diff and traced BinSkim post-analysis plus the only dependent validation path affected by compile success. Scan targets, reporting, cache behavior, and top-level concurrency are unchanged. A previously gated Linux x64 E2E job can now run once, which is intentional bounded completion of the SDK validation workflow, not a performance bug.
